> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **16** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2b1382a5b3887e4abd194411ef77a7cd368c95c2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `59fafbf4ea764b5012fbd684ca64b2f50a3c35ff` — the merge of head `4b4cfed7af4166806b44fcc6a4ec23c75c520300` into base `2b1382a5b3887e4abd194411ef77a7cd368c95c2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 59fafbf4ea764b5012fbd684ca64b2f50a3c35ff && git checkout 59fafbf4ea764b5012fbd684ca64b2f50a3c35ff
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2b1382a5b3887e4abd194411ef77a7cd368c95c2 4b4cfed7af4166806b44fcc6a4ec23c75c520300 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2b1382a5b3887e4abd194411ef77a7cd368c95c2 && git merge --no-ff 4b4cfed7af4166806b44fcc6a4ec23c75c520300

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2b1382a5b3887e4abd194411ef77a7cd368c95c2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2b1382a5b3887e4abd194411ef77a7cd368c95c2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a447bfdb8f2cf4237452adc0e3866074142de5ed`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/controlled-by-parent-every-master-edit.test.ts, .changeset/25044-cbp-every-master-edit.md + packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts, docs/adr/0055-master-detail-controlled-by-parent.md

Inputs: card #25044 (body and every comment through the dev report `6309719274`), PR #25066 (body, three-path file list, net diff against `main` at `a447bfdb8f`), the check-runs on that head, and the cited code read at the head. Face: `narrowing`, from the `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line on the body and in the changeset; `reviewFace` returns no path hit on this file list, so the floor is every diff path outside the prose faces, listed first above. Disclosure: the maintainer's ruling on #9387 (`5323310017`) governs this record — reach is stated abstractly; no probe, grant shape, request body, write-shape name for an unfixed path or served value is written here.

### ① Derived judgments

Governing text: ADR-0055 §3 (`docs/adr/0055-master-detail-controlled-by-parent.md:60`) — editing, deleting or creating a detail requires edit access to its master, and a create's master is read from the master id in the incoming body. Ruling B on #24932 (`6303721609`): no second spelling of a master scope while the mechanism moves to the engine leaf. Line numbers are the head's.

1. **The new question is a VERDICT, with no master set composed into the write — RIGHT.** `askBodyNamedMaster` (`security-plugin.ts:9237`) reads `opCtx.data[rel.fk]` as an own property, returns on a null and on a master already in `judged`, and otherwise calls the walk. It assigns nothing — not `opCtx.ast`, not `opCtx.options.where`, not `opCtx.data`; it throws or returns. `computeControlledByParentFilter` (`:8746`) carries no hunk, and the file list holds nothing under `packages/objectql/**` or `packages/spec/**`. Ruling B gets no second spelling.
2. **One walk, no second copy — RIGHT.** The closure's only callee is `assertControlledByParentChainEditable` (`:9435`), PR #25042's extraction; the diff adds no walk body, and `assertMasterRowEditable` keeps its single call site inside that walk (`:9476`). The predicate leg's loop is unchanged except that its result is bound to `predicateMasters` so the new question can read it (`:9272`–`:9280`).
3. **The refusal is the by-id leg's envelope, and nothing is written — RIGHT.** The walk is handed the gate's own `masterEditDenied` / `denyMasterEdit` (`:9205`–`:9219`): `PermissionDeniedError` (403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`), the sentence naming the caller's `operation` and `object`, the leg recorded beside the error in `MASTER_EDIT_DENIAL_LEG` (`:9214`). The gate runs in the security middleware's pre-phase (step 2.8, `:3246` and `:3256` for the delegator), which `executeWithMiddleware` (`engine.ts:6808`) runs before the executor, so a throw leaves the executor — hooks, strips, validation, the statement — unreached. The new pins compare the envelope to the live by-id refusal of the same caller and master, and read every row back unchanged.
4. **The insert's master is asked exactly once — RIGHT.** The insert branch reads `masterId` from `opCtx.data[rel.fk]` (`:9254`); `askBodyNamedMaster([masterId])` (`:9411`) reads the same key and returns on `judged.includes`. Pinned by the count test (the spy's fourth argument: one entry per insert). The same skip covers a by-id or predicate write whose body names a master already asked. One nit, not a hole: a body spelling the stored master in another scalar type is not `includes`-equal and asks the same master a second time — one verdict, asked twice.
5. **The fail-closed acceptance note is TRUE.** The gate reads the body before the executor's strips run: `stripReadonlyFields` / `stripReadonlyWhenFields` (`engine.ts:18109`, `:18143`, `:18428`; `rule-validator.ts:2117`) sit inside the `executeWithMiddleware` body (`engine.ts:17189`), and the `#19853` note at `engine.ts:4070` records that a master-detail FK that strip takes is a repoint that never lands. So a body naming a master the caller may not edit, on a reference the engine would strip, now answers 403 where the reference was dropped and the write landed. Refusing before the strip is the right side to err on; mirroring the strip rules in the gate would be a second copy of them, and the changeset's "What to do" covers the remedy.
6. **The changeset headline over-claims.** "a write to a `controlled_by_parent` detail asks for edit access on every master it involves" is a universal; the body under it is scoped ("for one shape of write … It now asks it of every master the write involves"). The dev's own report on the card (`6309719274`, out-of-scope findings F1 and F2; Acceptance note 1 on the PR) records two further readings in the same gate family, unchanged by this PR, so the diff does not make the universal true. It is the sibling's flag (PR #25042, whose headline was narrowed before landing). The PR title — the squash subject — and the `[#25044]` docblock sentence "on every shape it asks EVERY master the write involves" (`:9136`) carry the same universal. Flagged in ③.1; the changeset body, its Before / Now / Unchanged bullets and the ADR-0087 comment say only what the diff makes true.
7. **The accept-set change, read on the dispatch verdicts** (`resolveEngineUpdateDispatch` / `resolveEngineDeleteDispatch`, `:9264`–`:9271`): a by-id update whose body names a master other than the stored one is now judged on both; a predicate update is judged on each stored master of the rows the caller can read and then on the body's, only when at least one such row was reached (`:9280`); an insert, and a delete (whose `opCtx` carries no `data`, `engine.ts:20069`), answer exactly as before; a write the engine refuses on its own `reject` verdict is unchanged. On a delegated write both principals are asked (`:3256`). The changeset's Before / Now / Unchanged bullets match this reading, "Inserts and deletes" included.
8. **Scope held.** The hunks are inside `assertControlledByParentWrite` and the walk's docblock; `packages/objectql/**` and `packages/spec/**` are untouched; no governed path is in the file list (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` success).

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-security` `minor`, headline `fix(plugin-security)!:`, body `**BREAKING**`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and in the changeset, ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — RIGHT. The diff adds no export, no schema and no authorable spelling; it narrows the accept set of one write door, and no conversion carries it. Under the amended 「甲」 (`6303865025` on #6015, rule 2) such a narrowing ships now, in 18.x, as a BREAKING minor in the #24813 changeset shape — which this changeset is: Before / Now / Unchanged / What to do, with the remedy stated (a grant on the master, or a narrower write). The disposition is right: no metadata moves, so nothing for `migrate meta` to rewrite. `Check Changeset` reads success on the head. One wording flag on the headline (③.1); the level and the carriers stand.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Headline over-claim (①.6) — for the owning seat, before landing.** Narrow the changeset headline and the PR title to the shape the diff fixes, as the sibling's were; the docblock's universal sentence may go with them. A changeset-only hop is a prose-face move (`.changeset/` is on `REVIEW_SURFACE_EXCLUDED_PROSE_FACES`) and keeps this record; a docblock edit moves the reviewed file and re-owes it. Not a FAIL: the level, the carriers and the code are right, and the body text is accurate.
2. **Two further readings in the same gate family** (dev report `6309719274`, F1 and F2) — held out under the disclosure ruling; escalated to the seat by the dev. One further shape, read from the code of the gate and not measured, is held out under the disclosure ruling; escalated. None is changed by this PR, and none makes this diff wrong.
3. **Dev deviations — answered.** BASE moved twice (cut at `eddffc3390`, fast-forwarded onto `b2890909aa` after PR #25042 landed, merged with `72518d20f5`): the reviewed diff is the net diff against the merge base, three paths, and `main` has since gained one disjoint commit (`4bf079c693`). The throwaway validation on the pre-merge base committed nothing. The commit trailers follow AGENTS.md's model-free pair. Finding 1 is ③.2.
4. **`open_questions`: none declared.** The fail-closed acceptance note is ①.5 — judged true, noted, no carrier owed.
5. **Docs drift advisory** (`6309701002`): four hand-written pages name `SecurityPlugin` by symbol; none restates the body-master rule by its inputs. The lane seat's advisory, not a claim of this diff.
6. **Check-runs on the head.** Every `skipped` name is on `check-expected-skips.mjs`'s roster: the full-battery-only jobs (`Dogfood Regression Gate` matrix template, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Temporal Conformance`, `Console Pin Gate`), `Build Docs` on the `docs` filter, the two opt-in harnesses, and `Auto Label` / `Check PR Size` on a later `edited`/`labeled` event run beside their `success` on the `synchronize` run. `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` (aggregate), `Check Changeset` and the claim guards: `success`. `Test Core` (aggregate) and all six shards: `success`, read after the last shard completed. 47 check-runs, none pending, none red.
